theory.intro: A formal proof of congruence names the two triangles with their vertices in matching order, gives three pairs of equal parts — each with a reason — and finishes with the congruence test (SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS). Once triangles are proven congruent, matching sides and matching angles are equal, which lets you prove further results.
facts: Keep corresponding vertices in the same order: $\Delta ABC \equiv \Delta EDC$ means $A\leftrightarrow E$, $B\leftrightarrow D$ and $C\leftrightarrow C$.

Each line states one pair of equal parts with its reason. Common reasons are **given** (marked on the diagram), **common** (a shared side), **vertically opposite** angles, **alternate/corresponding angles on parallel lines**, and **equal radii** of a circle.
A shared side equals itself: write "$AC$ is common". In **SAS** the equal angle must be the **included** angle, between the two named sides.
Finish with $\therefore$ and the abbreviated test: **SSS**, **SAS**, **AAS** or **RHS**.

**Matching parts of congruent triangles are equal**: after proving congruence you may state that a pair of matching sides or angles is equal, and use it to prove lines equal, parallel, perpendicular, or a triangle isosceles.
steps: Name the two triangles with vertices in matching order.
List three pairs of equal parts, each with its reason.
State the congruence test that the three pairs satisfy.
If asked, use matching parts of the congruent triangles to draw a further conclusion.

foundation.solution_text:
In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CDB$:
$AB = CD$ (given)
$AD = CB$ (given)
$BD = DB$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CDB$ (SSS)

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta ADC$:
$AB = AD$ (given)
$\angle BAC = \angle DAC$ (given)
$AC = AC$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABC \equiv \Delta ADC$ (SAS)

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta EDC$:
$AC = EC$ (given)
$\angle ACB = \angle ECD$ (vertically opposite)
$BC = DC$ (given)
$\therefore \Delta ABC \equiv \Delta EDC$ (SAS)

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta ADC$:
$\angle ABC = \angle ADC = 90^{\circ}$ (given)
$AC = AC$ (common hypotenuse)
$AB = AD$ (given)
$\therefore \Delta ABC \equiv \Delta ADC$ (RHS)

In $\Delta OAB$ and $\Delta OCB$:
$OA = OC$ (equal radii)
$AB = CB$ (given)
$OB = OB$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta OAB \equiv \Delta OCB$ (SSS)

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta EDC$:
$\angle ACB = \angle ECD$ (vertically opposite)
$\angle BAC = \angle DEC$ (alternate angles, $AB \parallel DE$)
$BC = DC$ (given)
$\therefore \Delta ABC \equiv \Delta EDC$ (AAS)

In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CBD$:
$\angle ABD = \angle CBD$ (given)
$\angle ADB = \angle CDB = 90^{\circ}$ (given)
$BD = BD$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CBD$ (AAS)

development.solution_text:
In $\Delta AOB$ and $\Delta DOC$:
$OA = OD$ (equal radii)
$\angle AOB = \angle DOC$ (vertically opposite)
$OB = OC$ (equal radii)
$\therefore \Delta AOB \equiv \Delta DOC$ (SAS)
$\angle OAB = \angle ODC$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)
$\therefore AB \parallel CD$ (equal alternate angles)

In $\Delta PSQ$ and $\Delta PSR$:
$\angle PSQ = \angle PSR = 90^{\circ}$ (given, $PS \perp QR$)
$PQ = PR$ (given)
$PS = PS$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta PSQ \equiv \Delta PSR$ (RHS)
$QS = RS$ (matching sides of congruent triangles)
$\therefore S$ is the midpoint of $QR$

In $\Delta AED$ and $\Delta CEB$:
$AE = CE$ (given)
$\angle AED = \angle CEB$ (vertically opposite)
$DE = BE$ (given)
$\therefore \Delta AED \equiv \Delta CEB$ (SAS)
$\angle A = \angle C$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)

In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CBD$:
$DA = DC$ (given)
$\angle ADB = \angle CDB$ (given)
$DB = DB$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CBD$ (SAS)
$\angle ABD = \angle CBD$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)
$\angle ABD + \angle CBD = 180^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line $AC$)
$\therefore \angle ABD = \angle CBD = 90^{\circ}$, so $AC \perp BD$

In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CDB$:
$AB = CD$ (given)
$AD = CB$ (given)
$BD = DB$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CDB$ (SSS)
$\angle ADB = \angle CBD$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)
$\therefore AD \parallel BC$ (equal alternate angles)

In $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta ADC$:
$\angle ABC = \angle ADC = 90^{\circ}$ (given)
$AC = AC$ (common hypotenuse)
$AB = AD$ (given)
$\therefore \Delta ABC \equiv \Delta ADC$ (RHS)
$\angle BAC = \angle DAC$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)
$\therefore AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$

mastery.solution_text:
In $\Delta OAD$ and $\Delta OBD$:
$OA = OB$ (equal radii)
$AD = BD$ (given)
$OD = OD$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta OAD \equiv \Delta OBD$ (SSS)
$\angle ODA = \angle ODB$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)
$\angle ODA + \angle ODB = 180^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line $AB$)
$\therefore \angle ODA = \angle ODB = 90^{\circ}$, so $OC \perp AB$

In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CBD$:
$\angle ABD = \angle CBD = 90^{\circ}$ (given)
$\angle ADB = \angle CDB$ (given)
$BD = BD$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CBD$ (AAS)
$AD = CD$ (matching sides of congruent triangles)
$\therefore \Delta ACD$ is isosceles (two equal sides)

In $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta CBD$:
$AB = CB$ (given)
$\angle ABD = \angle CBD$ (given)
$BD = BD$ (common)
$\therefore \Delta ABD \equiv \Delta CBD$ (SAS)
$AD = CD$ (matching sides of congruent triangles)
$\angle ADB = \angle CDB$ (matching angles of congruent triangles)
$\angle ADB + \angle CDB = 180^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line $AC$)
$\therefore \angle ADB = \angle CDB = 90^{\circ}$, so $BD \perp AC$ and $AD = CD$ makes $D$ sit above the midpoint of $AC$
